TO:  Rental Housing Board Members

FROM:  Housing Protection Department

SUBJECT:  Establishing Temporary Relocation Assistance for Displaced Tenants

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Rental Housing Board Members take the following actions:
  1. Allow for a presentation of Temporary Relocation Assistance;
  2. Select a per diem rate for lodging from one of the following: a) General Services Administration
  (GSA) in the amount of $182; or b) Average lodging costs surveyed by Housing Protection staff
  using a 10 mile radius from the center of the City of Inglewood in the amount of $178.52;
  3. Approve the GSA established daily meal rates of $74 per person 13 years of age or older, and $37
  per person 12 years of age or younger;
  4. Approve daily pet accommodation rates of $37.50 per cat, and $68.60 per dog (two pet limit (cats
  and dogs only) per household;
  5. Establish a per diem for laundry services;
  6. Establish a per diem for storage; and
  7. Instruct the Housing Protection staff to submit a resolution with the findings for Temporary
  Relocation Assistance to be voted upon by the Board.

BACKGROUND:
The Housing Protection Ordinance (Ordinance No. 20-03) was adopted on November 5, 2019, and became
effective on December 5, 2019, providing eviction protection for tenants and capping rent increases of
multi-family properties (5 or more residential units on a parcel). The Ordinance was later amended in May
2021 (21-09).

Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the selection of the Rental Housing Board was initially delayed. However,
on June 13, 2023, the City Council nominated and appointed their respective nominees. Pursuant to
Inglewood Municipal Code section 8-123 (Relocation), if a tenant has vacated a rental unit in compliance
with a governmental agency’s order to vacate, or due to health or safety conditions, and regardless of
whether the owner has served a notice to temporarily terminate a tenancy, the owner shall pay temporary
relocation assistance to the displaced tenant household. The section further states that the temporary
relocation assistance shall be set by resolution of the Board. The amount may be based upon reasonable
per diem rates, which may include safe and sanitary hotel, motel, or short-term rental accommodations;
meal allowance if the temporary accommodations lack cooking facilities; laundry allowance if the rental
property included laundry facilities and the temporary accommodations lack laundry facilities; and pet
accommodations if the rental property allowed pets and the temporary accommodation does not accept
pets, and costs associated with moving and storage.

  DR-2

Establish Temporary Relocation Assistance
November 8, 2023

DISCUSSION:
Housing Protection staff researched various like sized municipalities to ascertain best practices regarding
regulations and the disbursement of temporary relocation assistance. As such, staff is recommending the
Board take action for the following per diem rates in the event temporary relocation is due to a displaced
tenant:

Lodging – May include safe and sanitary hotel/motel, or an Airbnb type of accommodation. If the owner
has a comparable vacant unit, the lodging per diem rate would not be due. The proposed per diem rates
were obtained from GSA ($182), and the data staff collected (average) when researching 3+ star rated hotels
within a 10 mile radius from the center of the city ($178.52).

Meals – The proposed per diem rates were obtained from GSA ($74, and $37), which are overwhelmingly
used by other municipalities.

Pet Accommodations - The proposed per diem rates ($37.50 per cat, and $68.60 per dog – limit two pets
per household <cats and dogs only>) were established by averaging facilities within a 10 mile radius from
the center of the city that offered pet accommodations.

Laundry Allowance – In the event laundry facilities are not included inside the unit, the Board may elect to
establish a per diem rate for laundry services.

Storage Allowance – Should a tenant’s displacement include the moving of items that require storage
facilities, the Board may elect to establish a per diem rate for storage.

Payment of the Temporary Relocation Assistance will be distributed weekly for days 1-30, and the tenant
is required to pay rent. For days 31-90, the owner is responsible for paying the rent differential to the tenant,
and the tenant is not responsible for paying rent. For days 91 and after, the owner is allowed to petition the
Board to change the Tenant’s temporary relocation case status to permanent relocation. The rent differential
is established by subtracting the tenant’s contract rent from the fair market rent for the unit size.

the Rental Housing Board into session at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Fragoso, Evans, and Brown; and
